messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: 1 object detected from 2 points
parts:
Just to add briefly to Tiago's comments:

Sometimes, point transect surveys are conducted on small study sites, in
which case points may be sufficiently close together for the same bird to
be recorded from more than one point, even if it doesn't move. This is a
mild violation of the assumption of independent detections, but the
methods are robust to much stronger violations, so this is of no concern.
It does not introduce bias. Consider these 3 cases:

1. A single bird is recorded twice from the same point on the same visit.
Counting a single visit as an effort of 1, this bird contributes twice to
the 'encounter rate' - birds detected per point per visit. But the effort
is only recorded once - a single visit. Hence double counting causes
bias.

2. A single bird is recorded once on each of 2 visits to the same
point. Hence the effort is 2, and although the bird is counted twice, its
contribution to birds detected per point per visit is just one, not two as
occurs in case 1. This doesn't generate bias.

3. A single visit is made to each point, and a bird is recorded once from
each of 2 points. Effort again is 2 (1 visit to each of 2 points), and
the bird is counted twice. Again, its contribution to birds detected per
point per visit is one, and this doesn't cause bias.

Steve
